question: A 14-year-old boy presents with painless cervical lymphadenopathy for 3 months, night sweats, and a 10% weight loss. Lymph node biopsy shows large binucleate cells with prominent 'owl-eye' nucleoli on a background of mixed reactive cells. Which diagnosis does this histology confirm?

answers.text: Burkitt lymphoma — high-grade B-cell NHL with starry-sky pattern

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Burkitt lymphoma shows a starry-sky pattern (macrophages engulfing apoptotic tumour cells) on biopsy, not Reed-Sternberg cells. It is the fastest-growing human tumour and presents rapidly, unlike this 3-month indolent course.

answers.text: Hodgkin lymphoma — Reed-Sternberg cells on mixed-cellularity background

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Reed-Sternberg (RS) cells — large binucleate cells with 'owl-eye' nucleoli — are pathognomonic of Hodgkin lymphoma. The mixed-cellularity background with eosinophils, plasma cells, and lymphocytes is the most common HL subtype in India. Constitutional B symptoms (fever, night sweats, >10% weight loss) help stage the disease.
T-cell lymphoblastic lymphoma typically presents with a mediastinal mass and TdT-positive blasts, not RS cells. It is managed similarly to ALL rather than classical HL.

answers.text: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma — large immunoblastic cells replacing nodal architecture

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: DLBCL does not produce RS cells. It shows large transformed B-cells replacing the lymph node architecture and is an aggressive NHL requiring different management from HL.

overallFeedback.feedback: The 'owl-eye' Reed-Sternberg cell on a mixed-cellularity background = Hodgkin lymphoma. Burkitt = starry-sky pattern; NHL subtypes do not show RS cells.

Correct! Reed-Sternberg cells (binucleate, owl-eye nucleoli) are pathognomonic of Hodgkin lymphoma. EBV is associated with ~40% of HL cases. B symptoms (fever, night sweats, >10% weight loss) indicate advanced disease.
